images.caption: Figure 1:MillBill overview.The language model revises a standard-practice machining plan; the geometric harness executes it, simulates the result and returns its deviations from the design. (1) The target B-rep. (2) AAGNet labels each face with a machining feature class (Sec.3.1). (3) Setups are chosen among the six axis directions by what the cutters can reach (Sec.3.2). (4) The model revises the operations, tools and cutting parameters of each setup, within the tool library and the machine limits (Sec.3.3). (5) The harness writes the toolpaths and G-code (Sec.3.4). (6) The simulated workpiece is compared with the design (blue: excess material, grey: within 0.1 mm, red: gouge), and the deviations go back to the agent (Secs.3.5and3.6).
Figure 2:Evaluation parts.Six of the 100 parts, grouped by the number of setups and labelled with their stock kind.

Figure 3:Simulated results.Four parts (rows): the target, the workpieces simulated from the programs of MillBill, the best code-writing agent (GPT-6 Astra) and CNC-Net, and the stock. Surface coloured by deviation from the design: grey withinτ=0.1\tau=0.1mm, blue excess material, red gouge.
Figure S1:Further simulated results.Five parts not shown inFig.3, laid out and coloured as there.

Figure S2:Failure cases.Target, MillBill’s simulated workpiece and the stock for three of the parts on which MillBill scores lowest (Acc0.1\text{Acc}_{0.1}of 64.5%, 78.3% and 86.5%,Tab.S5), coloured as inFig.3.
